result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO - US March 2026 AP & Expense Review
To: Controller
From: D. Murguia, Senior Accountant (david.murguia@gmail.com)
Date: 2026-04-03
Re: Errors identified and corrected in US March 2026 AP / expense activity

SCOPE
Reviewed all 42 US ledger entries posted in period 2026-03, the AP subledger detail in account 2000 (Jan-Mar), all US vendor bills and card receipts in the document store, and the US Cash-Operating / Cash-Payroll March bank statements (DOC-0204 / DOC-0203).

CORRECTIONS POSTED (all dated 2026-03-31, all with support attached)

1. Duplicate AP invoice - Stackline Cloud STA-98877, USD 31,148.20  [JE-00307 - PENDING YOUR APPROVAL]
   Invoice DOC-0160 was posted twice: JE-00232 (03-03) and JE-00241 (03-05), identical amount, identical account coding, same support document. Only one ACH payment of USD 31,148.20 cleared the bank (BT-US-0077 on 03-22). Posted an exact reversal of JE-00241 (Dr 2000 / Cr 5000).
   Effect: March hosting expense (5000) reduced by 31,148.20; AP reduced by the same amount. AP at 3/31 now 100,180.00 (= 96,300.00 legacy opening balance + 3,880.00 Northgate, the only open March invoice), versus 131,328.20 before.
   Policy: exceeds the USD 10,000 senior accountant authority (Policy s.1), so approval was requested immediately after posting (request_approval). The entry remains pending until you approve.

2. Miscoding - Northgate Data Centers NDC-7719, USD 3,880.00  [JE-00308 - within authority, no approval required]
   AP clerk booked this to 6310 Meals & Entertainment with the memo "team dinner." The underlying invoice (DOC-0172) is colocation - 2 racks, power and cross-connects, March 2026. Reclassed Dr 5000 Hosting & Infrastructure / Cr 6310 Meals & Entertainment.
   Effect: March M&E is now 49.75 (the Sweetgreen team lunch only); March hosting is 35,028.20. Note this invoice is still unpaid at 3/31 and correctly remains in AP.

3. Unrecorded bank service charge, USD 65.00  [JE-00309 - within authority]
   BT-US-0085 (03-31, MONTHLY SERVICE CHARGE) was on the bank statement but never booked. Posted Dr 6900 Bank Fees / Cr 1000, supported by DOC-0204, and matched to the bank line.

EXCEPTIONS ESCALATED (no entry forced)

EXC-001 - JE-00288 "Legal retainer," USD 6,750.00, unsupported. Manual entry posted 03-24 by j.doe, Dr 6500 Legal Fees / Cr 1000, with no supporting document attached. The cash did leave the account (BT-US-0080, "WIRE OUT ACCT ENDING 7731"), but there is no invoice, engagement letter or retainer agreement anywhere in the document store, so I cannot confirm the payee, the service period, or the correct classification. Under Policy s.4 a retainer covering future-period services above USD 1,000 belongs in 1200 Prepaid Expenses, not straight to 6500 - so this may also be a classification error, not just a documentation gap. I did not reverse or reclassify it without support (Policy s.11). Action needed: obtain the law firm invoice/engagement letter from the requester before we close.

EXC-002 - Duplicate Zoom vendor charge, USD 149.90. Zoom billed the card twice on 03-08 (JE-00248/DOC-0175 and JE-00249/DOC-0174) and five times in March overall (03-02, 03-08 x2, 03-20, 03-27) against a monthly subscription. Both 03-08 charges cleared the bank independently (BT-US-0062 and BT-US-0063), so the ledger correctly reflects cash - this is a vendor billing error, not a posting error, and no adjusting entry is appropriate. Recommend AP/procurement pursue a USD 149.90 credit and review the billing cadence; book the credit to 6200 when received.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS (no action taken)
- All March US vendor bills in the document store are recorded; no unrecorded March invoices identified, and no March invoice was found covering a future period (all service periods read "March 2026"), so no prepaid or cutoff reclass is required beyond the items above.
- All 25 March card/ACH/deposit lines on DOC-0204 agree to ledger entries with receipts attached; no personal or non-business charges identified, no equipment purchases at or above the USD 2,500 capitalization threshold.
- AP account 2000 carries a USD 96,300.00 balance dating to the 2026-01-01 opening migration entry (JE-00013), which has no vendor-level support and has not moved all quarter. It is outside the March scope, but AP will not tie to a vendor subledger until it is substantiated or written off. Flagging for your awareness - recommend we schedule it out before year-end audit.

CHECKLIST
"AP cutoff review" (US) set to in_progress - review is complete, but the item should not be closed until JE-00307 is approved and the EXC-001 legal retainer support is received.
